pullRequest.title: Add premium subscription features
pullRequest.description: Adds src/premium.ts: premium subscription model, payment processing, card validation, and tier-based pricing.
pullRequest.author: aksharguptaudacity

issues.title: Raw Payment Card Storage in Plaintext
issues.description: PaymentDetails interface stores sensitive payment card data (card numbers, CVV, expiry dates) in plaintext. This violates PCI-DSS compliance standards and exposes the application to severe data breach risks.
issues.suggestion: Remove card data storage entirely. Integrate with PCI-compliant payment tokenization services (Stripe, Square, PayPal, etc.) that handle sensitive data. Only store tokenized references: interface PaymentDetails { token: string; amount: number; }

issues.title: Missing Luhn Algorithm Validation
issues.description: Card number validation only checks length (16 digits) but doesn't perform Luhn algorithm validation, the industry standard for detecting invalid card numbers and typos. Invalid cards could reach payment processors.
issues.suggestion: Implement Luhn algorithm: function validateCardNumberLuhn(cardNumber: string): boolean { const digits = cardNumber.split('').map(Number); let sum = 0; for (let i = digits.length - 2; i >= 0; i -= 2) { let digit = digits[i] * 2; if (digit > 9) digit -= 9; sum += digit; } return (sum + digits[digits.length - 1]) % 10 === 0; }

issues.title: Sensitive Payment Data in Error Logs
issues.description: Payment card data is passed directly to database and logged in error messages (line 125). Sensitive payment information should never appear in application logs or error messages.
issues.suggestion: Never log card details. In error handlers, log only: console.error('Payment processing failed for user'). Mask card numbers in all outputs using only last 4 digits.

issues.title: No Idempotency Protection
issues.description: processPremiumPayment() has no idempotency check or request deduplication. Calling the function twice with identical parameters will charge the user twice, causing duplicate transactions.
issues.suggestion: Implement idempotency using request ID: export async function processPremiumPayment(userId: string, payment: PaymentDetails, tier: SubscriptionTier, idempotencyKey: string): Promise<boolean> { // Check if payment with this key already exists }

issues.title: Unsafe JSON.parse Without Error Handling
issues.description: JSON.parse() on line 149 has no try-catch block. If stored features JSON is corrupted or invalid, the function will throw an unhandled exception and crash the application.
issues.suggestion: Wrap in try-catch: const features = (() => { try { return JSON.parse(subscription.features); } catch { return []; } })(); Or validate features type before parsing.

issues.title: Unvalidated JSON Data Structure
issues.description: subscription.features is stored as JSON string but its structure and content are never validated. Malicious or corrupted data could be stored and parsed.
issues.suggestion: Validate features array: function validateFeatures(features: unknown): string[] { if (!Array.isArray(features) || !features.every(f => typeof f === 'string')) { return []; } return features; }

issues.title: SQL Injection Risk from Unvalidated userId
issues.description: No input validation for userId parameter before database queries. If userId is user-controlled and not properly sanitized by database driver, it could be vulnerable to SQL injection.
issues.suggestion: Validate userId before use: if (!userId || typeof userId !== 'string' || userId.trim().length === 0) { throw new Error('Invalid userId'); }

issues.title: Year 2000 Offset Bug in Expiry Date
issues.description: Expiry date validation uses hardcoded 2000 offset (2000 + parseInt(year)). This fails for cards expiring after 2099 and creates ambiguity for YY format dates.
issues.suggestion: Use proper date parsing: const currentYear = new Date().getFullYear() % 100; const cardYear = parseInt(year); const fullYear = cardYear > currentYear ? 2000 + cardYear : 2100 + cardYear; Or better: require YYYY format.

issues.title: N+1 Query Pattern in hasFeatureAccess
issues.description: Multiple consecutive database queries without batching. Each feature access check makes a full subscription query. With many users, this causes performance degradation.
issues.suggestion: Cache subscription data with TTL instead of querying each time. Use Map or Redis with 5-minute TTL to avoid repeated database hits for the same userId.

issues.title: Hardcoded Tax Rate Ignores Jurisdiction
issues.description: Fixed 8% tax rate is hardcoded and doesn't account for user location or tax jurisdiction requirements. Tax varies by region (0-25%).
issues.suggestion: Define configurable tax rates by region: const TAX_RATES = { 'US': 0.08, 'CA': 0.13, 'EU': 0.19 }; Implement geo-based tax calculation based on user location.

issues.title: Generic Error Handling
issues.description: Generic catch block logs error but doesn't distinguish between different failure types (network error, database validation error, duplicate payment, timeout).
issues.suggestion: Implement specific error handling: catch (error) { if (error.code === 'UNIQUE_VIOLATION') { /* Handle duplicate */ } else if (error.code === 'CONNECTION_ERROR') { /* Handle network */ } throw error; }

issues.title: Hardcoded Feature Lists
issues.description: Feature list for each tier is hardcoded in upgradeUserSubscription(). Changes require code modification and deployment. No dynamic way to add new features.
issues.suggestion: Move to database or configuration: const TIER_FEATURES = { premium: ['unlimited_todos', 'priority_support', 'custom_themes'], enterprise: [...] }; Or query features from database based on tier.

issues.title: Insufficient Error Information
issues.description: processPremiumPayment returns boolean but doesn't indicate whether failure is due to validation, insufficient funds, or gateway error. Caller cannot distinguish recovery strategies.
issues.suggestion: Return detailed result: interface PaymentResult { success: boolean; reason?: 'invalid_details' | 'insufficient_amount' | 'gateway_error'; message: string; }

issues.title: Inefficient Database Query
issues.description: getUserSubscription uses SELECT * when only specific columns needed. No verification of indexes on user_id column.
issues.suggestion: Specify exact columns: const query = 'SELECT user_id, tier, valid_until, features FROM subscriptions WHERE user_id = $1'; Ensure user_id has unique index in database schema.

issues.title: Missing Runtime Type Validation
issues.description: Tier parameter lacks runtime validation. TypeScript enums are erased at runtime. Invalid tier values could reach critical functions.
issues.suggestion: Add runtime validation: const VALID_TIERS = ['premium', 'enterprise'] as const; function validateTier(tier: unknown): tier is Tier { return VALID_TIERS.includes(tier); }

refactorings.summary: Significant architectural improvement needed through design patterns and separation of concerns

suggestions.title: Extract PaymentProcessor Class
suggestions.description: Consolidate payment validation, charging, and price calculation into dedicated PaymentProcessor class. Currently scattered across multiple functions.
suggestions.currentState: Validation (validatePaymentDetails), charging (chargeCard), and pricing (calculateSubscriptionPrice) are separate functions
suggestions.targetState: class PaymentProcessor { validateDetails(payment: PaymentDetails): boolean; async charge(payment: PaymentDetails, amount: number): Promise<boolean>; calculatePrice(tier: SubscriptionTier): number; }
benefits: Centralized payment logic for easier security audits

suggestions.title: Extract SubscriptionManager Class
suggestions.description: Group subscription operations (upgrade, access control, retrieval) into SubscriptionManager class for better cohesion.
suggestions.currentState: upgradeUserSubscription, hasFeatureAccess, getUserSubscription are separate functions
suggestions.targetState: class SubscriptionManager { async upgrade(userId: string, tier: SubscriptionTier): Promise<void>; async hasFeatureAccess(userId: string, feature: string): Promise<boolean>; async getSubscription(userId: string): Promise<Subscription | null>; }
benefits: Supports future features like downgrade or cancellation

suggestions.title: Implement Strategy Pattern for Pricing
suggestions.description: Replace hardcoded pricing logic with Strategy pattern to support multiple pricing models and regions.
suggestions.currentState: Tier-based pricing tightly coupled with tax and fee calculations

suggestions.title: Implement Repository Pattern
suggestions.description: Extract all SQL queries into SubscriptionRepository class following Repository pattern.
suggestions.targetState: class SubscriptionRepository { async savePayment(payment: Payment): Promise<void>; async updateSubscription(subscription: Subscription): Promise<void>; async getSubscription(userId: string): Promise<Subscription | null>; }

suggestions.title: Implement Validator Pattern
suggestions.description: Apply Validator pattern with composable validators for payment details. Replace multiple if-statements with independent, reusable validators.
suggestions.currentState: Multiple if-statements checking card number, CVV, and expiry date
suggestions.targetState: class CardValidator { private validators = [new CardNumberValidator(), new CVVValidator(), new ExpiryDateValidator()]; validate(payment: PaymentDetails): ValidationResult; }
benefits: Easier to add new validation rules

suggestions.title: Extract Configuration Constants
suggestions.description: Centralize all magic numbers and strings (pricing, tax rate, fees, validation rules, features) into configuration object.
suggestions.targetState: export const SUBSCRIPTION_CONFIG = { pricing: { premium: 9.99, enterprise: 49.99 }, tax: { rate: 0.08 }, payment: { processingFee: 0.029 }, validation: { cardLength: 16, cvvLength: [3, 4] }, features: { ... } };
benefits: Easier to update pricing and rules

suggestions.title: Extract Feature Assignment Logic
suggestions.description: Extract feature array assignment and subscription date calculation into separate functions.
suggestions.currentState: Feature array logic and date calculation mixed within function
suggestions.targetState: function getFeaturesForTier(tier: SubscriptionTier): string[]; function getSubscriptionExpiryDate(): Date;

suggestions.title: Create SubscriptionTier Type Alias
suggestions.description: Replace repeated 'premium' | 'enterprise' union types with single type alias.
benefits: Single source of truth for tier types

suggestions.title: Eliminate Duplicate Row Parsing
suggestions.description: Extract repeated subscription row parsing logic into mapper function.
suggestions.targetState: function mapRowToSubscription(row: any): Subscription { return { userId: row.user_id, tier: row.tier, validUntil: new Date(row.valid_until), features: parseFeatures(row.features) }; }
benefits: Single source of truth for data mapping

The code must NOT be merged to production without addressing critical issues.
